question: Which of the following antitumor agents acts forming a covalent and irreversible complex with the thymidylate synthase and its cofactor, previous activation to the corresponding deoxynucleotide?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "5-Fluorouracil" -> "converted to 5-fluoro-2'-deoxyuridine monophosphate (FdUMP)" -> "FdUMP forms covalent complex with thymidylate synthase" -> "inhibits DNA synthesis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Methotrexate" -> "inhibits dihydrofolate reductase" -> "decreases tetrahydrofolate" -> "decreases thymidylate synthase activity" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Cyclophosphamide" -> "converted to active metabolites" -> "forms DNA cross-links" -> "inhibits DNA replication" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Taxol" -> "stabilizes microtubules" -> "prevents mitotic spindle disassembly" -> "inhibits cell division" -> 60%
analysis: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is an antitumor agent that is converted into its active form, 5-fluoro-2'-deoxyuridine-5'-monophosphate (FdUMP). FdUMP forms a covalent and irreversible complex with thymidylate synthase and its cofactor, 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate, inhibiting the synthesis of thymidylate, which is essential for DNA replication and repair. This mechanism is specific to 5-Fluorouracil among the options provided.
